findings.text: A globally visible atomic counter tracks how many zero pages are currently placed by sharing. It starts at zero and is the only cross module counter in this lane.
Safe range walk over one virtual area first checks that the supplied operation table is allowed and rejects disallowed tables, otherwise it forwards to the unsafe range walk with identical arguments.

Unsafe range walk over one virtual area builds a walk descriptor from the given area and private token, rejects empty ranges and ranges outside the area or without an address space, then applies the requested locking discipline to the address space and area before walking.
Advisor context carries four members for wall clock start and prior duration and smoothed ratio and accumulated processor time, named start_scan and scan_time and change and cpu_time.
Advisor selector offers a disabled mode and a scan time driven mode, with the selector variable residing in static storage and therefore beginning in the disabled mode.
Default scan batch is 100 pages, with the live scan batch variable starting at that default and the sleep interval between scans starting at 20 milliseconds.
Hash width for the address space slot table is 10 bits.
Exponential smoothing weight for scan time adaptation is 30 percent new sample with the remainder carried from history.
Advisor processor floor is 10 percent, with companion tunables starting at 70 percent ceiling and 200 target scan time units and 30000 pages upper bound and 500 pages lower bound.
Run control uses stop 0 and merge 1 and unmerge 2 and offline 4, with the live control variable starting in stop.
Node merging scope has two build variants that both report merging enabled and a single node identifier, with only the frame to node mapping differing across builds.
Stable and unstable trees each have a dedicated singleton root array of length one, and the live root pointers begin aimed at those singletons.
Duplicate stable nodes are recognized by a sentinel head value derived from the migration anchor list, distinct from ordinary list heads and tree parents.
The slot list head is self linked and empty at boot with the scanner cursor parked on it, while the three object caches for reverse map items and stable nodes and slots begin null until slab setup.

Operational counters for scanned and shared and sharing and unshared pages plus reverse map population plus chains plus duplicates plus skipped pages all start at zero, while the zero page checksum and zero page enable flag are read mostly and start cleared.
Chain pruning interval starts at 2000 milliseconds and per page sharing cap starts at 256 with smart scanning starting enabled.
Advisor defaults form two states where disabled restores the default batch size while scan time mode clears accumulated timing state and restarts from the minimum batch size.

Scan start is recorded only while the scan time advisor is active, with the previous duration helper substituting the current measurement when no history exists and the smoothing helper blending history and current sample by the configured weight.

While scan time advising is active, completion of a scan pass adapts the next batch size toward the target scan duration within processor use bounds, using floored wall time and floored processor share plus a target ratio and a smoothed change ratio, with results clamped by per page cost and global limits before context update.
A mutex serializes scanner thread control and a spinlock protects the slot list.

Slab setup creates reverse map then stable node then slot caches, unwinding earlier caches on failure and reporting allocation failure, while teardown releases in reverse order and marks the slot cache absent.
A stable entry is a chain exactly when its list length field holds the chain marker, and a duplicate exactly when its head field holds the duplicate sentinel.

Attaching a duplicate tags it with the sentinel and queues it on the chain and bumps the duplicate tally, while detaching removes it from its queue or tree and drops the tally, clearing the head marker under debug builds.

Reverse map allocation returns zeroed objects without retry or warning and counts successes globally, while release drops both global and per address space tallies and clears the owner for debug safety before returning the object.
Stable node allocation may dip into emergency reserves to avoid stalls under pressure, while release requires an empty node unless it is a chain.
An address space counts as exiting when its user reference count has reached zero.

The break scan recognizes present shared pages and migration entries resolving to shared folios without waiting and placed zero page entries, reporting the first matching address in the examined range while skipping absent entries.
Two walk operation tables share the same entry scanner but differ in locking discipline, one requesting shared address space and area protection and the other requesting exclusive area protection.

Unsharing a range repeats locate then fault until no shared page remains or a terminal fault status appears, converting out of memory status into an allocation failure and otherwise reporting success.

Concurrent access bit updates can force a fault retry and truncation races can surface as bus errors that still satisfy unsharing, while memory cgroup pressure can surface as out of memory leaving transient uncounted pages recovered by later scans.

Merge eligibility excludes shared or shareable or huge mappings and droppable mappings and mappings with special flags and direct access file mappings and architecture specific protected mappings, with the area wrapper applying the same test to the area file and flags.
A mergeable area lookup succeeds only for a live address space where the address lands in an area marked mergeable and backed by an anonymous reverse map structure.

Copy on write breaking drops the reverse map owner reference and clears overlay index state before taking shared address space protection to locate the area and unshare a single page, then releases protection.

Mergeable page lookup holds shared address space protection while resolving the area and folio, accepts only anonymous non device memory with an added reference, flushes processor specific views on success, and always releases protection.
Frame to node attribution collapses to node zero when cross node merging is enabled, otherwise it follows the frame physical node.

Chain promotion swaps a fresh chain node for the colliding duplicate in the tree, with empty duplicate queue state and current prune time and chain marking plus a bumped chain count, and thereafter guarantees queued duplicates are write protected with identical content.
Chain release removes the chain from its tree and frees it and drops the chain tally.

Stable node removal preserves sharing accounting with non tail queue members affecting the sharing tally and the tail affecting the shared tally, while each member also decrements its address space merging tally and releases its owner reference with cleared overlay state and page aligned address, and the node leaves whichever owner holds it with sentinel layout validated at build time.
Folio acquisition offers three locking disciplines with no lock and blocking lock and non blocking attempt.

Stable folio acquisition validates the tagged mapping before and after reference and lock acquisition, reports busy without blocking when the non blocking discipline finds contention, retries when the node frame number changed under migration ordering, and otherwise discards the stale node and reports absence.

A zero reference count usually means the folio is free or a tail page and implies staleness, except for brief freeze windows and swap cache migration where the node must be retained, with mapping and swap cache checks plus ordered recheck of the frame number separating those cases.
Stable node allocation can stall under reclaim pressure and therefore draws on reserves, while reverse map allocation instead fails fast without retry or warning.
